I'm mapping out which cells belong to color 4, tracing the outline shapes row by row to figure out the bounding boxes for each object.

Testing whether 4's cells form a filled diamond centered around (7,7) with radius 5 — but the interior contains background zeros, so it fails the occlusion check and must stay as an exact outline shape instead.

Now I'm tracing color 8's cells, which look like a right-triangle outline with a full top row and a left column descending down the grid.

I confirm the diagonal matches a "top-left" triangle orientation: top row at r=1 spanning c2-c13, left column at c2 spanning r1-r12, and a diagonal connecting them that hits every expected cell (r7→c7, r9→c5, r10→c4, r11→c3, r12→c2). So 8 is confirmed as a tl-triangle outline spanning rows 1-12, cols 2-13.

Now I'm mapping out color 5's cells across rows 6 through 12, tracking which columns are filled to figure out its shape.

I determine that 5 forms a rectangle outline spanning rows 6-13 and columns 6-14, confirmed by checking row 6 and row 13's boundaries. With all three masks now defined (8 as triangle outline, 4 as its exact visible cells, 5 as rectangle outline), I move on to figuring out their front-to-back stacking order by comparing edges.

No visible 8 cells fall inside 4's or 5's mask regions, so 8 has no outgoing edges. But visible 4 cells at row6-8 column 2 align with 8's left column, giving 4→8, meaning 4 sits in front of 8.

Checking further, a visible 4 cell at row6 column 12 lands on 5's top edge and another at row12 column 6 lands on 5's left edge, so 4→5 as well, putting 4 in front of both shapes. Then checking visible 5 cells against 8's mask, the one at row6 column8 falls on 8's diagonal, giving 5→8.

That leaves edges 4→8, 4→5, 5→8, so the paint order by indegree is 4, then 5, then 8 on top. Now I'm laying out the 15x15 grid, starting with the exact 4 cells row by row.

Still writing grid coordinates...

Continuing to trace through rows 7-10, tracking where the 4s, 5s, and 8s overwrite each other in each column position.

Rows 11 and 12 fill in similarly, resolving overlaps by keeping the later value in the sequence, while row 13 becomes all 5s across columns 6-14 and row 14 ends up empty.

Excluding row5 itself, the diamond occupies rows2-8, cols2-8, so I'll paint the line first across the full row, then overlay the diamond shape on top: row2 has col5, row3 cols4-6, row4 cols3-7, row5 cols2-8, row6 cols3-7, row7 cols4-6, row8 col5, leaving the line visible at cols0-1 and cols9-10.
